Plawno Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Pławno, Poland

Not demolished. Jews settled in Pławno no later than the 18th century, with major community growth in the 19th; by 1921, 566 (36%) were mostly murdered at Treblinka in 1942. This cemetery, undocumented on an 1839 topographic map but confirmed via 1845-1846 parish burial-fee records, certainly dates to the first half of the 19th century; it remained active until WWII, receiving victims of German oppression including Rabbi Icek Rabinowish and the Haberman family (killed 1939 at a local estate park) and at least 13 people killed at nearby Kruszyn that same year. Destruction likely began during the war and continued for decades. In the late 1980s-early 1990s, the Gidel Friendship Society began maintaining the site, building a lapidary from preserved matzevot alongside a 1993 memorial stele reading 'Memory place for Jews resting here - members of our community. Gidle 1993.'
